changes: p1: father's name normalized as Deva (Devabhaṭṭa) with title 'bhaṭṭa' (the colophon spells it 'bhaṭa'), following the rule that titles are stripped; as_written now quotes the colophon exactly
p3: 'dhullopākhya' is a surname statement ('whose surname is Dhullo'), so the title is now 'Dhullo (surname)' rather than the compound; the stray 'pra' before sadāśiva is flagged
p3: confidence lowered to medium because 'vibhage' is corrupt (for vibhāge) and the name carries a stray prefix
purpose cleared: 'vibhāge' records how ownership came about (a share of property), not why the copy was made; this is moved to notes

notes: The author is Ratnākara Pauṇḍarīkayājin, son of Devabhaṭṭa. The colophon's 'pauṃḍarīkapājiralākara' is a corruption of 'pauṇḍarīkayāji-ratnākara'. The catalogue lists Sadāśiva Bhaṭṭa as the scribe, but the colophon only says 'pustakam idaṃ dhullopākhya-[pra?]sadāśivabhaṭṭānāṃ vibhāge': this book fell to the share (vibhāga, as in a division of property) of Sadāśiva Bhaṭṭa, whose surname is Dhullo. He is therefore an owner, and nothing says he copied it. The 'pra' before 'sadāśiva' is unclear. It may be a misreading of an honorific (e.g. śrī/paṃ) or part of the surname (e.g. 'dhullopākhya-pra-'). The colophon gives no date, scribe or place of copying.
